title: Toast: As in browned bread
summary: Josh and Chuck open the year with a celebration that the show's listeners passed one million dollars raised for the Cooperative for Education (CoEd) in Guatemala, then devote the episode to toast: its history from ancient Egypt and Rome through medieval cinnamon toast, Welsh rarebit, Victorian toast recipes (bone marrow toast, toast sandwich, toast water, milk toast), toasting implements from toasting forks to the GE D12 and Charles Strite's pop-up toaster, the nichrome heating element, the Maillard reaction and its health concerns, toast around the world, the artisanal avocado toast trend, and the origin of "toast" as a drinking salute and slang. The episode ends with a listener mail segment about a soldier and her son who fall asleep to the show, and a correction about Zoog Island and the Edmund Fitzgerald episode.

segments.title: Opening banter and CoEd million-dollar milestone
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck welcome listeners back for the first episodes of the year and announce that listeners raised over one million dollars for CoEd, a Guatemalan education cooperative that helps break the cycle of poverty.

segments.title: Hosts' toast preferences and breakfast experiments
segments.summary: The hosts discuss whether anyone dislikes toast, and Josh describes making oat nut wheat toast in a Breville toaster oven, with butter kept in a butter bell and cinnamon honey on top, following a listener suggestion.

segments.title: Ancient origins and medieval toast
segments.summary: The hosts cover the probable origins of toast in ancient Egypt, the Latin root of the word toast meaning scorched, medieval golden sops, and the invention of cinnamon toast in Naples.

segments.title: Welsh rarebit and Victorian toast recipes
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Welsh rarebit and its rabbit-name legend, then turn to Victorian Britain's toast craze, including a bone marrow toast recipe from a book attributed to Charles Elme Francatelli and a toast sandwich from Mrs Beeton.

segments.title: Toast water, milk toast and thin Victorian toast
segments.summary: The hosts describe toast water, made by steeping toast in boiling water, and milk toast, a New England dish of toast with warm milk and sugar or syrup often given to invalids, which inspired the comic strip character Casper Milk Toast. They also note Victorian toast was cut much thinner.

segments.title: Mid-episode break
segments.summary: The hosts take a short break before moving on to toasting implements.

segments.title: Toasting implements and the toast rack
segments.summary: The hosts trace toasting tools from toasting forks through stove-top toast racks, and discuss the toast rack as a tool for holding toast so it does not get soggy.

segments.title: Electric toasters, nichrome and the GE D12
segments.summary: Albert Marsh's nichrome alloy, a nickel and chromium heating element, is described as the basis of electric toasters. The hosts discuss the GE D12, an early mass-marketed toaster that required flipping the bread.

segments.title: Pop-up toaster mechanism and Charles Strite
segments.summary: Charles Strite's pop-up toaster, marketed as the Toastmaster, is discussed, including the mechanism that replaced an early timer with a bimetallic strip and electromagnet and capacitor circuit that releases the toast.

segments.title: Conveyor toasters and the Balmuda toaster
segments.summary: The hosts praise conveyor belt toasters used in sub shops and hotel breakfasts, then discuss the Balmuda steam toaster, a Japanese appliance that uses steam to crisp the outside of bread.

segments.title: Maillard reaction and toast browning
segments.summary: The hosts explain the Maillard reaction, the chemical reaction between amino acids and sugars that gives toast its flavor and color, note that alkaline bread browns more easily than sourdough, and mention health concerns about charred foods.

segments.title: Toast around the world
segments.summary: The hosts list international toasts including Kaya toast from Singapore and Malaysia, Italian garlic toast, Swedish toast skagen, Spanish pan con tomate, Australian and British fairy bread, and toad in the hole.

segments.title: Avocado toast fad and toast slang
segments.summary: The hosts discuss the artisanal toast trend that started in San Francisco with Julietta Correlli and the origins of toast as a drinking salute, plus slang uses like toast meaning finished and the Ghostbusters line attributed to Bill Murray.

segments.title: Listener mail: falling asleep to the podcast and a correction
segments.summary: A correction to the Edmund Fitzgerald episode says Zoog Island is in the Detroit River, not Lake Michigan. Then a listener named Anna from Cleveland writes that she and her son fall asleep to the show, and the hosts respond.

segments.title: Sign-off
segments.summary: The hosts close the episode and remind listeners how to send mail.
